Remaining work

Task allocation

Acemoglu and Restrepo (2019) follows labor demand through changing task assignments, which motivates tracing preparation across the household and office boundary.

When a household brings its records to a tax office, the preparer may receive an unsorted collection of statements or a file organized around a question that the household has already investigated with AI. Comparing those submissions for the same underlying matter allows us to follow the work moved across the office boundary, including the time saved when a calculation arrives with supporting records that the preparer can use.

For the household deciding whether to purchase help, preparation changes the cost of the remaining service while discovery can change the reason for buying it. Through the task-allocation perspective in Acemoglu and Restrepo (2019), we follow the work assigned to people and machines across the household and office boundary as customers finish some operations and bring different remaining questions to professionals.

Better information also directs professional attention toward matters where resolving an issue has greater expected value, with purchased work following the household’s decision after that information arrives. We count customer time and inference resources alongside the office’s basic and expert hours, following Becker’s allocation-of-time analysis, so the economic comparison includes the preparation performed before a fee is paid.

For a household close to purchasing help, a completed calculation can lower the remaining bill enough to bring the case into the office, even as each purchased case requires fewer hours. When another household completes the entire matter at home, its professional demand disappears, so adding the arriving files requires following both participation and the amount of work contained in each purchase.

Interpreting an explanation

Unaided learning

Bastani et al. (2025) compares practice assistance with later unaided mathematics performance, showing why the design of help matters for retained ability.

For a junior preparer reviewing a completed calculation, an explanation can depend on knowing how the underlying transaction fits the supporting records, so the route from documents to an answer can teach something that the answer alone leaves unresolved. We represent the needed foundation by a hidden sign BBB and the principle used in a later judgment by a hidden sign TTT, with one observation revealing BBB imperfectly and a relational explanation revealing their product BTBTBT imperfectly.

When the foundation remains unknown, either target sign fits the observed product because changing both hidden signs preserves the explanation. After processing both observations, the learner can multiply them to cancel the foundation, leaving information about the target through the remaining noise, which explains why a stronger explanation has more educational value when its recipient understands the records on which it depends (fig. 2).

Within this calculation, foundation reliability rBr_BrB​ and explanation reliability rAr_ArA​ determine later unaided prediction error through 1−rB2rA21-r_B^2r_A^21−rB2​rA2​, while receipt probability ppp determines how often the learner processes the pair. As either reliability improves, a received pair becomes more informative, and increasing access passes that gain to more learners, with prior error normalized to one in the figure.

At zero foundational reliability, either possible foundation remains equally plausible, so increasing explanation reliability alone leaves the learner’s target uncertainty unchanged. Once the foundation carries information, improving the explanation has a positive return, and a person who already knows the foundation can use the explanation immediately, giving the same material different educational value according to the knowledge brought to it.

Within a high-school mathematics experiment, Bastani et al. (2025) found that ordinary AI assistance improved practice performance while subsequent unaided performance fell, and a tutor designed to safeguard learning largely mitigated that loss. We follow retained information through the case for the same measurement reason, while instruction that reveals TTT directly supplies another route to the principle.

Preparing the figure

Diagnostic cases

Learning with assistance

Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond (2025) finds experience-dependent gains and evidence of worker learning in customer support, connecting useful assistance to the recipient’s prior knowledge.

Across the returns reaching an office, a diagnostic case reveals a distinction that changes how a junior worker handles a later matter, while a familiar calculation may add little understanding. In customer support, Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond (2025) finds larger assistance gains among less experienced workers together with evidence of learning, giving an empirical reason to track received guidance and prior experience when studying what work teaches.

To follow that learning into professional entry, we focus on a qualification margin where a fully revealing occasion allows an eligible novice to pass an unaided assessment. Aggregating retained diagnostic occasions gives a transition flow MMM, measured in newly acquired qualifications per unit of time, while the qualified population share EEE counts people who can perform the assessed judgment independently.

Allocation matters because a revealing occasion creates a transition only when it reaches someone who still needs the qualification, and the benchmark assigns such occasions to eligible novices. Under random contact across the entire occupation, the eligible share is 1−E1-E1−E, so a contact rate m(c)m(c)m(c) produces M=(1−E)m(c)M=(1-E)m(c)M=(1−E)m(c), with repeated exposure yielding less additional entry as more people become qualified.

Because the object counted is an acquired ability, sending the same lesson to an already qualified person leaves the expert headcount unchanged, while sending it to an eligible novice can add someone able to perform the assessed judgment. Obsolescence can later return that person to the novice group, keeping receipt, learning, and continued possession of qualification connected through the population account.

For measurement, the path from a customer file to MMM runs through case arrivals, diagnostic content, actual recipient exposure, and subsequent unaided assessment, allowing a study to identify which part changed. Pages 4–5 of the paper develop these definitions, and Appendix A gives the signal calculation behind the figure.

Paying for practice

Once the junior preparer can carry acquired qualification to another employer, an informative placement has a private value tied to future professional earnings. Writing the value of qualification as Δ\DeltaΔ, a case with transition probability mmm supports a learning payment Δm\Delta mΔm, which the novice can finance through a separate payment or a wage concession within the service arrangement.

Competition passes this contribution into the fee charged to the household, allowing the office to cover its basic and expert labor bills while charging less for a case that teaches someone. When preparation removes the diagnostic occasion, it removes that learning discount along with some current work, so the household’s saving depends on both the labor avoided and the private value of the lost experience.

For two ways of handling the same matter, retained diagnostic material can consequently support a lower customer payment even when its processing uses additional time. We weigh that time against the novice’s expected qualification gain, with the credit following the person who receives and processes the information and the preparation resources remaining part of the service’s total cost.

Through that payment, the supporting material in an ordinary tax file enters an investment decision whose return extends across filing seasons. Following the novice’s career then reveals how purchased instruction responds to a changing flow of experience and how the resulting expertise enters the prices faced by later households.
